Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. home.headline: Lamar Jackson told Ravens he’s coming back this season, report says
home.blurb: Injured quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return later this season, the NFL Network reported Sunday, citing anonymous sources. NFL Network reported that Jackson is undergoing surgery to repair a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand. Jackson’s injury typically takes at least six weeks to recover from, though it could take up to nine weeks, the report said. That would line up with a potential return during the Ravens’ four straight AFC North matchups to end the regular season, beginning Dec. 20 at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Perhaps the Ravens still have hope. “Just stay alive” was the paraphrase of Jackson’s message that he delivered within 24 hours of suffering a significant thumb injury on his throwing hand against Buffalo, the report said. After starting 4-1 with Jackson under center, Baltimore has slipped to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North, facing long odds to make the postseason. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on the offense’s first play of his first game back from an ankle injury in a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury against Buffalo, were placed on injured reserve before Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , meaning they will miss at least four games. Jackson has not spoken to reporters since the injury, and coach Jesse Minter has declined to share details about it or Jackson’s potential recovery timeline. “I’m not going to speak on that,” Minter said when asked about Jackson on Thursday night. The Ravens have made plans to move forward without their two-time NFL Most Valuable Player this season, acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. Though neither side disclosed the terms, Baltimore is reportedly sending Arizona a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for the 33-year-old veteran and a 2027 fifth-round selection, ESPN reported. Brissett has started 73 of 109 games and completed 62.1% of his passes with 86 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. He also has 17 career rushing touchdowns. He is 23-50 as a starter. The move came about 12 hours after Baltimore’s embarrassing loss to the Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and struggled mightily with a heavily bandaged right ankle. He completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards and was intercepted twice. home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

The Ravens won't trade Henry before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL deadline despite falling to last in the AFC North. The decision follows a 33-10 defeat to Jacksonville that left the Ravens at 4-5 and searching for answers without Lamar Jackson . Henry hasn’t begged for a lifeline or tried to bail on a season gone sideways. "I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said after Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The loss marked four straight defeats, and the Ravens haven't gone five straight without a win since 2007. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around,'" he continued. When asked how the Ravens plan to turn things around, Henry shook his head and said, "We have to." "It’s the only thing we can do. Go back to work and try to get it going." In each of Baltimore's last three losses, the team gave up 30 points. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest. Falcons vs. Bengals prediction Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11. In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. NFL Power Rankings NFL predictions: Fireworks between Falcons and Bengals CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 23: Ja'Marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals is tackled by Darren Hall #34 of the Atlanta Falcons at Paul Brown Stadium on October 23, 2022 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Knight · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:34 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Falcons squandered a golden opportunity to take control of the NFC South in Week 8, falling completely flat in a bad weather game against the Bucs. Now sitting at 3-5—along with the rest of the division—Atlanta is in a difficult place. Games against some of the AFC and NFC's best await over the next month, sandwiched around the team's Week 11 bye. The first game in this sequence comes early Sunday morning in Madrid, as the Falcons take on the Bengals. Cincinnati is a bit volatile, but possesses one of the best offenses in the NFL led by quarterback Joe Burrow and the elite receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Right now, the Falcons are 3-point underdogs against the Bengals, per FanDuel. Atlanta needs a victory to stay afloat in the playoff hunt, but can it come against this Cincinnati team? Let's take a closer look. Falcons vs Bengals Week 9 predictions The Bengals hold the NFL's second-best scoring offense, best third-down offense, and are also top-10 in total yardage. This will be one of the biggest tests for Atlanta's defense all season. The good news for the Falcons is that Cincinnati's offense is very one-dimensional, with the vast majority of their production coming via the passing game. Over the past few weeks, Atlanta's biggest issue has been stopping the run. That shouldn't be a problem in Week 9, as the Bengals are 30th in rushing yardage and 28th in yards per carry. So all eyes then turn to the Falcons ability to slow down Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. I'm not sure how well the Falcons will fare, but having their full complement of cornerbacks available will be a big help. A.J. Terrell, C.J. Henderson, and Billy Bowman are back in the lineup together for the first time since September. Joe Burrow has been fantastic, but he's still vulnerable to pressure. With the Falcons (hopefully) getting star edge rusher James Pearce Jr. back in the lineup this weekend, the pass rush is the best path to victory. Atlanta has been outstanding generating interior pressure and pretty solid outside, but has lacked a true finisher to pile up sacks. Pearce brings that ability, and will hopefully bring a big boost to the defensive line on passing downs. On the other side of the ball, the message is simple: the Falcons offense must get back on track, and can't afford to start slow. Michael Penix Jr. is coming off a career-worst performance in a monsoon against the Bucs. The Bengals defense has been opportunistic and good at limiting scoring, but gives up a ton of yardage. This will be the softest defense the Falcons have faced in weeks, and they must take advantage. Atlanta will need a good day from Penix and the passing game to keep pace with Burrow, but the biggest player to watch is probably Bijan Robinson. This game has the potential to be a "Bijan takeover" performance, with Cincinnati 29th in yards per carry allowed on defense. Bijan got a bit stuck in the mud against Tampa Bay, and I think he'll have an explosive game in Madrid. All in all, it likely comes down to the Falcons ability to limit the Bengals offensive chances by holding the ball as much as possible, and capitalizing on their own scoring opportunities. Cincinnati is beatable—the game last week against the Titans showed that—but you have to be able to keep up with them offensively. away.headline: Ja’Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR’s Status Before Falcons Matchup
away.blurb: For fantasy managers, the evidence supports treating Chase as available, and the Week 9 slate offers little reason to sit him. The final inactive report remains the last confirmation before kickoff, and no verified report currently suggests a restriction. The bigger problem sits with Atlanta. Higgins is coming off a 155-yard afternoon, and Chase just produced 141 yards of his own. Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns through seven games. If the full group is available Sunday, the Falcons have to defend a passing attack that spreads the ball without moving away from its top receiver. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR's Status Before Falcons Matchup Skip to content NFL Search Search NFL Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR's Status Before Falcons Matchup Nishat November 4, 2026 Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'marr Chase (1) walks for the lockeroom after the NFL Week 8 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. The Bengals played to a 43-36 overtime win against the Titans. Ja'Marr Chase enters Week 9 in Madrid off the best receiving afternoon of his season. He caught 11 passes for 141 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans , and he found the end zone in that same game. The only open question was whether the short turnaround to Spain changed anything. Cincinnati's latest injury report answered it. Chase is not listed on the Week 9 injury report. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Gives Bengals WR Clear Status The Bengals left Chase off their Wednesday report entirely. That report was only an estimate because the team held a walkthrough instead of a full practice, but it did not carry any new designation for the club's top receiver. Chase also made the trip. The offense is a high-octane attack, striking for big gains and playing at one of the fastest paces in the land. Meanwhile, the defense is a bunch of rusty lawn chairs, making every opposing passer look like an All-Pro arm. Jones and this offense are back home for just the second time in six weeks and face a Cowboys secondary near the bottom of almost every pass defense metric. And as bad as Dallas is at defending downfield, it's equally as stinky stopping the run. The Colts' defense is just as rotten. Colts Preview The Colts have lost four in a row entering Week 9, fresh off a 42-7 blowout loss against the Jaguars . After trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , this team looks demoralized. Head coach Shane Steichen is a virtual lock to be fired by the end of the season, perhaps even earlier. We're likely to see them trade both Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs as well. Even in a home game against a poorly coached Cowboys team, I prefer fading the Colts in this spot. Cowboys vs Colts Spread Pick to Make I'm taking the Cowboys -5.5 over the Colts here. They took care of business in a game they were favored to win in Philly, when they won handily 38-21. It wouldn't surprise me to see something similar against the Colts. This is a great spot for the Cowboys offense to get rolling, as Indianapolis has allowed 42, 16, 26, and 34 points during this losing streak. In this stretch, the Colts are 23rd in Dropback EPA and 26th in Rush EPA. This may be a spot where the Cowboys can get their running game going. I like getting below the key number of six here, so we'll ride with the Cowboys -5.5 against a tanking Colts team. This is a must-win game for Dallas as they try to keep pace with the Giants in the lowly NFC East. Picks: Cowboys -5.5 (-115) Cowboys vs Colts Player Props I'm targeting the Cowboys' running game in player props, going with Javonte Williams Over 70.5 rushing yards . Williams was inefficient against the Cardinals, but back in Week 7, he rushed for 155 yards against the Eagles, so it's not like he's been completely unproductive lately. While it's a high bar at 70.5, the Cowboys are projected to play with a lead as 5.5-point favorites, which would mean more rushing volume. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news
away.source: Dallas Cowboys | Official Site of the Dallas Cowboys
away.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Roughly two weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys were feeling great about their injury report as key players began to get healthy and return to the practice and playing field. In the blink of an eye, they're suddenly back to having a lengthy and growing list of injuries that will again cost them impact players going forward. PJ Locke missed time this season before returning and suffering a concussion in Week 8, clearing protocol ahead of the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts before suffering a second concussion in as many weeks and, this time, he will not return in only a week's time. On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys officially ruled Locke out of the looming contest against the San Francisco 49ers — a sign he will likely miss multiple games. It was a scary sight to see Locke lying motionless for several moments before being helped to the sideline and not being permitted to return at Lucas Oil Stadium. Turpin will join DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), those three were ruled out ahead of kickoff against the Colts, in the rehab group this week to determine if either of them can go against the 49ers. And with Ferguson down, the expectation is that Luke Schoonmaker will return from injury to help with the currently ailing tight end depth chart. And though Marist Liufau was activated from injured reserve last week, Malachi Lawrence recently joined Thompson on IR, leaving the Cowboys with only one IR-DTR (designated to return) spot this regular season, assuming Lawrence returns as expected. That means if Ferguson, Goodson and Locke are moved to IR, only one of them would be allowed to return unless the Cowboys make the playoffs. On the day of the NFL's trade deadline, Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that he is not expecting Dallas to make a significant trade, "but don't count it out." In pulling out a much-needed win in Indianapolis, the Cowboys seemingly took craziness to a whole new level. After challenging his defense to execute for a full 60 minutes, Quinnen Williams led by example with a dominant performance that helped the Cowboys finish strong and close out a crucial victory. home.headline: Colts send six-time Pro Bowler to 49ers ahead of NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The six-time Pro Bowler has been a focal part of the Colts offense in 2026 with fellow wideout Alec Pierce limited to two games this season due to injury. The longtime former member of the Los Angeles Chargers will join an injury-ravaged wide receivers’ room in San Francisco, with pass-catchers Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans both currently nursing ailments. Christian Kirk and rookie wideout De’Zhaun Stribling are also still on injured reserve, and 2024 first-round pick Ricky Pearsall is out for the season. Tuesday’s trade continues a fire sale for Indianapolis, as the Colts also recently shipped out DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson. NFL fans will find out soon if the likes of Taylor , wide receiver Josh Downs and quarterback Daniel Jones could be joining Allen on his way out of Indianapolis. The Indianapolis Colts are continuing to reshape their roster ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, with wide receiver Keenan Allen set to join one of the league’s top contenders. Indianapolis has agreed to trade Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a sixth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The deal is contingent on the 34-year-old receiver passing a physical. Star running back Jonathan Taylor’s name has been swirling in rumors for weeks, but the Colts are trading another player away with multiple Pro Bowl nods to his credit. Allen is in first season with 2-7 Indianapolis after signing with the club in mid-August. Allen leads Indianapolis in targets (58) and receptions (40) this year while ranking second in receiving yards (351) as well, despite missing one contest. He added another career achievement Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, catching four passes for 26 yards and moving past Hall of Famer Tim Brown for eighth place on the NFL’s all-time receptions list. Allen now has 1,095 career catches. The move may give Allen his long-awaited shot at a Super Bowl ring. Through his time with the Chargers, plus the 2024 campaign with the Chicago Bears, he’s played in just six playoff games and has never advanced past the divisional round. The 49ers enter Week 10 tied with the Buffalo Bills for the best record in football at 7-1. Keenan Allen Faces Unresolved Legal Case Allen also faces an unresolved legal matter stemming from an August 30 arrest. He faces preliminary misdemeanor charges related to operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Indianapolis police said officers observed signs of intoxication after encountering Allen during a traffic investigation and determined that his blood-alcohol level was nearly three times the legal limit of 0.08. No trial date has been set. Allen could also eventually face discipline from the NFL, although the league typically waits for the legal process to conclude before taking action. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Jets: NFL Week 9 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On the heels of consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs are back at home and have a lighter game in the 12:00 p.m. local slot against the New York Jets. Just because New York doesn't have the makings of a playoff contender doesn't mean it can't give Kansas City a fight, though. The Chiefs know as well as any team that self-inflicted errors are the easiest way to hand a game over, so the hosts will have to put the pedal to the metal in order to secure a resounding triumph. With kickoff just hours away, will it be the Chiefs or Jets that emerge with a victory? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 9 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: While there's only so much the Chiefs can truly prove against the 2-6 Jets, this is a game Kansas City simply has to win. A two-game losing streak to a pair of playoff teams is one thing. A home loss to a franchise that’s still a year away from even making the “in the hunt” playoff graphic? That would be disastrous. I’ll be watching to see if the Chiefs’ pass rush can wrangle Geno Smith, who is tied for the second-most sacks taken among quarterbacks this season, while hoping to see more from rookie R Mason Thomas in that effort. Will the Chiefs’ banged-up defense be able to hold down a lively group of weapons, even without Garrett Wilson, or will the KC offense need to score more than 24 points for the first time since before the bye week? I could see a bounce-back stat line for Kenneth Walker with another explosive play or two from the star running back. Jordan Foote: The Chiefs typically have at least one game a year they have no business losing and somehow just don't seem to show up for. While it's possible that this is the one, it absolutely cannot be the case. Coming off ugly losses to the Seahawks and Broncos (for different reasons), this is a squad that desperately needs to rebound in a hurry. Fortunately, the matchup is there in Week 9. The Jets' offense has had its shining moments, although it's virtually impossible to trust this version of Smith to go toe-to-toe with Patrick Mahomes if he's on his game. Add in that Kenneth Walker III may be due for another statement performance, and it's hard to see anything other than turnovers or penalties making this too close of a game, in my view. Tyler Brown: The Jets have been more competitive than their 2-6 record suggests, with five of their six losses coming by one score, and Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise. They can be dangerous on offense, with wideouts Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell playing well lately and running back Breece Hall returning, even as Braelon Allen's rushed for 565 yards. This is also a real test for tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore, who will face pass rushers David Bailey and Will McDonald IV. On the other hand, New York’s defense has been giving up production to opposing tight ends, which sets up Travis Kelce and Noah Gray well. Andy Reid can wear the Jets down with Kenneth Walker and, in a perfect world, let Patrick Mahomes work the secondary off that. Smith is also among the league’s worst at turning pressure into sacks, so a Chiefs pass rush that's been waiting for a game like this should hypothetically get home a few times. Neither team will run away, and the Jets will stay in it for a while. But Kansas City is the more talented team and needs the win more. Coming to town are the New York Jets, who may be 2-6 but have numerous one-score losses that hint at this team being better than its record indicates. As expected while the 2026-27 NFL campaign approaches the trade deadline , neither of these clubs is close to fully healthy. Could that factor into how Week 9's game unfolds? Perhaps, especially with several high-profile players missing this weekend's contest. With that in mind, here's who's inactive for Kansas City and New York in Sunday's matchup. Kansas City Chiefs inactives vs. New York Jets Here are the Chiefs’ inactives for today’s game against New York: CB Mansoor Delane QB Garrett Nussmeier FB Ben VanSumeren DE Jack Pyburn OT Diego Pounds DT Peter Woods CB Mansoor Delane QB Garrett Nussmeier (emergency third quarterback) FB Ben VanSumeren DE Jack Pyburn OT Diego Pounds DT Peter Woods The Chiefs' injury situation was pretty bleak a week ago when a pair of cornerbacks were ruled out for an eventual defeat to the Denver Broncos. L'Jarius Sneed went on the injured reserve list , with No. 6 overall NFL Draft pick Mansoor Delane also sitting with a lingering shoulder issue. The latter injury remains a problem in Week 9, as head coach Andy Reid revealed on Friday that the star rookie would be inactive once again. In the same Friday media availability, Reid ruled defensive tackle Peter Woods out. Woods, who left Week 8's outing with a neck injury after just three snaps, didn't practice all week. Two other injury notes for the Chiefs pertain to supporting players on the depth chart. Special teams ace Nikko Remigio kicked off the week as a limited participant in practice but progressed to full participation in time to carry a questionable designation into Sunday. He's good to go. On defense, second-year tackle Omarr Norman-Lott was limited for another week and ruled out on Friday. Norman-Lott has one more week left in his 21-day evaluation window after being designated to return from the physically unable to perform list. He isn't listed among KC's inactives due to technically still not being on the active roster. On Saturday, the Chiefs activated defensive tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad via standard elevation. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson headlines the list, as he remains in concussion protocol and didn't practice all week. Elsewhere, players like linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin), defensive end Joseph Ossai (ankle) and cornerback Nahshon Wright (back) are also missing in action. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, who's been battling an ankle injury, was deemed questionable after not participating in Wednesday and Thursday's practices before getting a full workload on Friday. NFL Power Rankings Two Bold Predictions for the Kansas City Chiefs vs. New York Jets in Week 9 Ryan L. Dodson · Athlon Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:16 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return home Sunday to face the New York Jets after dropping two straight games. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been bottled up in the defeats after leading the league in rushing through his first five games. The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos limited K9 to a combined 105 rushing yards on 35 carries. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Kenneth Walker Tops 100 Yards The Jets have allowed the seventh-most rushing yards to opposing running backs through eight weeks. Walker topped 100 yards on the ground in four of the first five games of the season. Even after averaging just 3.0 yards per carry the last two games, he's still second in the NFL with 5.5 yards per carry. Two weeks ago, the Jets allowed Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards on 25 carries . Walker is a clear upgrade from Gordon and will gash the Jets on the ground. The Chiefs' passing game has also had its issues. Tight end Travis Kelce has been managing an ankle injury, and they'll look to run the ball often. Bold Prediction No. 2: Chiefs Defense Records 2+ Sacks The Chiefs' pass rush has been much maligned, and it's for good reason. They're tied for last in the NFL with nine sacks on the season. Defensive tackle Chris Jones, who is one of their leading pass rushers, has just a half-sack on the season. Defensive end George Karlaftis reached the quarterback in Week 8 for his team-leading second sack of the season. The Jets are tied for second with 23 sacks allowed on the season. Quarterback Geno Smith has been sacked at least twice in the last seven games. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is known for his relentless blitzing, and the Chiefs will get home two or more times.

NFL Power Rankings Chiefs-Jets betting line & game prediction: KC looks to get back on track Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid orchestrates the action against the Las Vegas Raiders during a Week 4 NFL game at Allegiant Stadium in Paradise, Nevada on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. (Joe Camporeale/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Pete Sweeney · Kansas City Star Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs and New York Jets both need a win. Last week, the Chiefs suffered their second straight loss as the Denver Broncos rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to win 28-24. The Jets suffered their third consecutive loss Sunday, falling 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -9.5. Behind the NYJ-KC matchup Although their goals and expectations entering the season were different, Sunday's Chiefs-Jets game represents a fork in the road for both teams. The Chiefs entered 2026 hoping to rebound from a 6-11 season and return to the Super Bowl conversation, but their loss to Denver has turned simply winning the division into a dogfight. At the same time, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show tangible progress in his second season — or his tenure in New York could be short-lived. A home matchup against the two-win Jets presents the Chiefs with the classic get-right opportunity. Their best path to doing so lies in reestablishing the ground game. New York is 21st in the league against the run in opponent yards per game (123.6), allowing 4.0 yards per carry. During his first five games, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker averaged 133 rushing yards per game. Walker rushed for just 105 yards combined in the losses to Seattle and Denver, but he still ranks third in the NFL with 770 rushing yards. Kansas City will also look for ways to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more after his breakout performance of 143 scrimmage yards against the Broncos. "He's a super-talented player, and he just brings joy," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said of Johnson. "He has the right mindset, the right energy, and he wants to be great. Obviously, we have Kenneth, and he's such a special football player — but to have someone that can come in whenever Kenneth's tired or needs a break at all, and he can bring energy and juice, too, I think that's a special combination those guys have there." Mahomes suggested the Chiefs need to find additional touches for Johnson, potentially through an expanded role in the passing game. Johnson's 73-yard receiving touchdown highlighted Mahomes' 321-yard, three-touchdown performance in the loss. Kansas City's passing game also saw a breath of fresh air with wide receiver Rashee Rice's return to the lineup. Rice caught a team-high seven passes on eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He also appeared to have the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter before the play was nullified by a false-start penalty . Reestablishing the ground game with Walker and Johnson could create opportunities for Rice, tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Xavier Worthy against a veteran Jets secondary that has recorded just one interception this season. Still, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid respects Glenn's defensive scheme and personnel. "They've got some good veteran guys — whether it's the safeties, the linebackers," Reid said. "So you're not going to have things that are botched up. Sometimes, you get coverages that are kind of messed up a little bit and there are holes there. They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. And they've got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys." A Jets player to watch is rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who missed his team's Week 8 game because of a groin injury. Bailey leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, more than a quarter of the team's 20 sacks this season. Reid said there's a "good chance" left guard Kingsley Suamataia returns to the starting lineup after being benched for the second time in four games because of a "coach's decision." The Chiefs' short-yardage and goal-to-go woes have been under criticism this week after a loss in Denver could have been different by dialing up a quarterback sneak. Perhaps this is the week Reid adds it back into the playbook at long last. Despite New York's disappointing season, quarterback Geno Smith has put together his own resurgence, entering Sunday with 1,913 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. Smith has posted a passer rating above 100 in five of his last six road games, and the Jets have gained 377 and 439 yards of offense in their past two games. Against a quarterback playing so efficiently, the Chiefs will need to generate more pressure than they did against the Broncos. Pro Football Focus credited Kansas City with just five pressures against Denver's Bo Nix. While wide receiver Garrett Wilson's status remains in concussion protocol, running back Breece Hall could return after missing five games. In Hall's absence, Braelon Allen has been a fantastic replacement, recording at least 100 scrimmage yards in the last four consecutive games. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, acquired by New York from Indianapolis in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts, established a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Raiders. Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane missed Sunday's game after aggravating his shoulder injury but returned to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. Delane's return is more important given Smith has been brilliant at throwing the deep ball, with 565 yards gained on passes of 20-plus air yards. Defensive end George Karlaftis said Wednesday that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has preached the importance of developing a "killer instinct" after his unit's forgettable recent fourth quarter. "No matter what the call is, you just got to find a way to finish," Karlaftis said. "So I think, especially against a divisional opponent, against a great team that Denver is, when you're up, when you're leading, no matter what that lead is, you got to find a way to win the game as a defense. "And I know I felt that. I know the guys in the room, players and coaches, really felt that. And I think that's something we're going to take with us and harp on for the rest of the season." Reid confirmed Wednesday that Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker against the Jets despite his 54-yard miss against Denver. Butker had made three extra points and a 45-yard field goal before pushing his final kick wide right. The Chiefs can get back on the right path and build some confidence by handling the Jets. The problems — an inconsistent pass rush, short-yardage struggles and too many penalties — have been glaring. This is a good opponent to fix all three against. Jets-Chiefs game prediction Beyond the Chiefs' advantages in record, quarterback and overall outlook, I think this matchup gives Kansas City an opportunity to tap back into the offensive identity that worked early in the season — establishing Walker on the ground to open up everything else. Defensively, clean up the penalties and get to the quarterback. We've heard plenty about pressures, but Smith has been sacked 23 times this season — tied for second-most in the NFL. If not Sunday against the Jets, then when? The Chiefs use their get-right game to do just that. Winner: Chiefs 24, Jets 13 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney's record: (5-2-0) | Against the spread: (2-4-0)

NFL Power Rankings Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the New York Jets — in their first matchup since 2023 — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 206 Jets are likely more focused on evaluating head coach Aaron Glenn — and the likelihood of having a trio of top ten selections in April's NFL Draft — than what happens the rest of the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 9.5-point home favorites. Although the Jets lost to the Las Vegas Raiders 38-33 in Week 8, Gang Green did rack up 439 yards of offense, including 166 rushing yards. New York should not be considered a pushover opponent. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) It's been a hard fortnight to be a Chiefs fan. I am still of a mindset to see how this team looks at the end of the season, but losing any of the next three games would be catastrophic for the season. Earlier on, I was worried about the Chiefs sleeping on a team like the Jets. But after losing two straight games, I think the Chiefs will come out and play one of their best games of the season. The concern will remain of what happens against good teams, but I don't think you will see a play with their food performance at Arrowhead following a tough two-game road trip. Chiefs 31, Jets 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) After consecutive losses, the Chiefs badly need a win to get back on track. The Jets are a far cry from as bad as they have been in recent memory, but the Chiefs should win this game with minimal issues. The Jets are more talented offensively than they have been in some time, but running back Breece Hall has missed time this season with injury, and wide recieve Garret Wilson has shown up on the injury report. With a quality defense ranked near the top in several categories, the Chiefs will need to bring their A-game. Kansas City played a solid game offensively, but this week all eyes will be on the short-yardage and red zone situations where the team failed to convert in critical spots last week. Defensively, a turnaround game for the pass rush would be a big boost.I would continue to watch the emergence of Emmet Johnson alongside Kenneth Walker in creating a two-headed monster in the KC backfield. Chiefs 26, Jets 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think the Chiefs are gonna handle the Jets at Arrowhead this week. If Garrett Wilson can't go, the Jets lose their best threat in the passing game, and Spags can load up on the run and make them beat Kansas City through the air. If Mahomes gets the Chiefs up two scores early, I don't see how the Jets keep up. I think this one gets out of hand in the second half. Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs enter a three-game stretch that feels critical to keeping their AFC West title and No. 1 seed hopes within reach. After starting 5-0, Kansas City has dropped two straight, and the losing streak needs to stop Sunday against the Jets. New York has remained competitive, but this is a team the Chiefs should beat, especially back at Arrowhead in front of a crowd eager for something to celebrate. Garrett Wilson's uncertain availability could hurt the Jets, although Braelon Allen has proven their running game deserves respect regardless of Breece Hall's status. For Kansas City, getting Kenneth Walker III going starts with making defenses respect the passing game again. To me, his recent struggles go beyond the running back and offensive line. Tyquan Thornton's absence has taken away a deep threat, allowing defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage. The Chiefs must find ways to stretch the field without him, create room for Walker and get back to building off play-action. I expect Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid to find those answers this week, with Kansas City settling down and delivering a convincing win. Chiefs 27, Jets 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The New York Jets come to town at a pretty good time for the Chiefs. Having lost the past two games, they'll be hungry to get back in the win column. Andy Reid has rightfully been blamed for the team's failures over the last couple of weeks, so I'd expect at least a "B" game plan on Sunday. He should let Kingsley come back as the left guard, and Rashee Rice is getting healthier— these two developments alone could get the offense moving enough to beat the Jets. But the Chiefs also have developing weapons in Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen. Both rookies should continue to see increased touches every week from here to the postseason (in my humble opinion). I'm of the opinion that the Chiefs are still in pretty good shape overall— the Denver loss hurt, but KC looked like the better squad. The Jets aren't as bad as their record either, so this won't be a cakewalk, but I expect the home crowd will have plenty to cheer about. Chiefs 28, Jets 13 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I hope the Chiefs are as angry as the fan base after that last game. Because they need to play angry, even against the Jets, if they're going to turn this season around. Now in a fight for the division, the Chiefs must take advantage of these next three games against what seems like inferior opponents. While I have serious concerns about this football team, I believe they get back in the win column this weekend. The offense should be able to get in a rhythm and right some of their wrongs from the past two weeks. And for the Jets, if Garrett Wilson can't go, then I think the Chiefs' defense should hold their own and focus on shutting down their running game. Chiefs win fairly comfortably in this one. Chiefs 28, Jets 17 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) It's been a rough couple of weeks. The Chiefs have lost back-to-back games. But they played well enough in Denver that they should have won that game. Some poor coaching decisions and a few mental lapses are all it takes in the NFL to lose to a division rival. That being said, this should be a get-right game for the Chiefs. The New York Jets are having a very Jets-like year and have struggled to move the ball and score points. They are also averaging 123.6 yards allowed per game on the ground. The Chiefs should plan on dealing a healthy dose of Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson to them. This could be the perfect get-right game for Kansas City. Chiefs 24, Jets 10 Nate Christensen The Jets have been a better team this year. Their offense has dramatically improved with Geno Smith at quarterback and an impressive set of weapons. Braelon Allen has broken out at running back. Adonai Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Omar Cooper have formed a good trio. They have good young tight ends and two top-10 draft picks at tackle. Their offense can score and keep them in games The issue has been their defense, which is bad. They don't have a lot of talent, particularly in the secondary. I think the Chiefs should easily be able to throw the ball this week, and I expect Kenneth Walker to bounce back with a big game. Chiefs 34, Jets 23 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) Welcome to Game 1 of three that the Chiefs are fully expected to win, similar to the first five games of the season. The Jets are talented on offense and competitive on defense; they have too many recent first-round picks not to be, but there's nothing Aaron Glenn and company can do about Kansas City needing a confidence-building win after two straight losses. Look for the Chiefs' run game to come alive again and marry it to a passing attack that found answers against the Broncos last week until the final play. Whether the wide receivers are a big part of the game plan, I see Kansas City lighting up the scoreboard and putting this game out of reach in the second half. Nate now moves into second place among our three 6-1 contributors. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: New York Jets rule out superstar WR for matchup vs. Kansas City Chiefs NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed that the New York Jets will be without star wide receiver Garrett Wilson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9. Wilson — who started his professional career as the No. 10 pick in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft — has been in the league's concussion protocol and missed all of New York's practice sessions ahead of the Jets' tilt against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. The 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year started his tenure in New York with three 1,000-yard seasons as the Jets' top wideout, but saw his production dip when injuries derailed his 2025 campaign with the Jets.

away.headline: Jets vs Chiefs: Garrett Wilson headlines Jets’ inactives
away.blurb: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

home.headline: Report: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes avoids major elbow injury
home.blurb: "Patrick took a pretty good shot to the throwing arm today and came off the field in some pain. We checked him out right away and he told us his elbow was sore, but he was determined to get back out there," Reid said. "He returned, made some throws, and kept competing the way he always does. He's one of the toughest players I've ever coached, and he doesn't like missing snaps." Nov 09 (Field Level Media) - Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury to his right elbow, according to a media report Sunday night. An MRI exam revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling over the next few days, leaving his status uncertain for next Sunday's game against the host Atlanta Falcons. Mahomes injured his throwing arm during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half. "From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes said. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't -- hopefully, I haven't done the test yet -- it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff." Mahomes was drilled by Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey while raring back to fire a pass downfield with 1:33 left in the first half. He came off the field supporting his right elbow with his left arm and appeared to be in significant pain. Head coach Andy Reid said the Chiefs would follow all of the proper steps to confirm Mahomes is not hurt. If upcoming tests give the Chiefs pause, Reid said the plan will be to "prepare Justin (Fields)" to face the Falcons on Sunday. Fields did not attempt a pass Sunday but ran twice for minus-1 yard. Mahomes returned to start Week 1 after sustaining a season-ending left knee injury in 2025.

Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. away.headline: Lions LB Jack Campbell 'determined' to play football again: Live updates, injury news
away.blurb: Aidan Hutchinson told CBS Sports' Melanie Collins that it wasn't hard to get motivated this week, pointing out that it was weird without Jack Campbell in meetings. Campbell's medical diagnosis has not yet been made public. Medical experts reached by USA TODAY did point out the uniqueness of Campbell's post-injury symptoms, saying that delayed recovery of upper-body movement could be associated with central cord syndrome . It's a rare medical condition common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell’s head and neck at impact. A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football. Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season. The Detroit Lions took the field in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins without a key member of their defense – Jack Campbell. It marked the Lions' first contest since the linebacker suffered a terrifying neck injury during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . The injury left Campbell laying on the field motionless before being carted off the field on a backboard as emotional teammates looked on . Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body. It was an encouraging update that extended beyond the generic ones provided earlier in the week . From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. The Lions escaped Miami with a 19-9 win over the Dolphins, but it was clear that Jack Campbell was still top of mind. "A lot of what we said was win No. 6 for 46," Dan Campbell told reporters . "And we did that today. We got that done." EXCLUSIVE: Rare diagnosis could explain Lions LB Jack Campbell's neck injury update, spine experts say On Nov. 7, the Lions announced they were placing the linebacker on injured reserve. It's a reminder that Campbell has a long way to go in his recovery, but he remains determined to get back on the field, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins. "He is determined to get back on this football field, telling Dan Campbell: 'Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back,'" Collins reported on the CBS broadcast of the game. away.blurb: While Campbell obviously isn't out of the woods yet, that is at least a shred of good news. We'll continue to be on the lookout for more updates. Jack Campbell injury update: Latest news on Lions LB's status after Week 8 game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Yahoo Fantasy Forecast | NFL Trade Deadline Reactions TRENDING NFL trade deadline tracker Mike Moraitis · The Sporting News Wed, November 4, 2026 at 12:30 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Detroit Lions have a major concern with linebacker Jack Campbell after the Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings . Campbell suffered a neck injury in the fourth quarter of the contest and was down on the field for several minutes in what was a very scary scene. Players on both teams were showing clear concern for Campbell's well-being as he was tended to on the field by medical personnel before he was eventually placed on a stretcher and driven off on a cart. Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Campbell's status. UPDATE: The Lions provided an update on Campbell hours after the game and revealed that he is now resting at a local hospital and will remain overnight for further evaluation and monitoring. "Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them." UPDATE: Head coach Dan Campbell provide an update on Jack Campbell after the game, revealing that the Lions linebacker was breathing and alert when he left the stadium, but that was all he could offer at the moment. "Dan Campbell says Jack Campbell was breathing and alert when he left the stadium but had no further updates," Al Karsten of Pride of Detroit wrote. UPDATE: The Lions announced that Campbell has been taken to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. "Jack Campbell is being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury," the Lions said. According to ESPN's Kevin Seifert , Campbell was placed on a backboard and has been lifted onto a cart and is being taken off the field following his injury. "Jack Campbell has been moved onto a cart and the entire Lions team is headed over to surround him before he leaves," Seifert wrote. Here's a look at the play in which Campbell got hurt. We can only hope Campbell is going to be OK. We'll update this page as soon as more information is known. home.headline: Dolphins' Zach Sieler Reportedly Played with Torn Biceps vs. Lions, Latest Rumors on Injury Status
home.blurb: Bleacher Report • 2h Vikings WR Calls Out Haters 😶 Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season with a torn biceps, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter . Schefter reported the injury occurred on the first play of Miami's 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Sieler proceeded to log 50 more snaps on defense and special teams. The 31-year-old has been a stalwart along Miami's defensive front since first signing with the team midway through the 2019 season. He has appeared in 110 total games for the Dolphins. Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury As expected, this is a rebuilding year for Miami, which is tied for the NFL's second-worst record (1-7). Because of that, Sieler looked like a possible trade candidate prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. That option is obviously off the table now. If the Dolphins believe they can make a quick turnaround in 2027, they may continue to see Sieler as an important piece of the defense. General manager Jon-Eric Sullivan might instead view his three-year $64 million extension a little differently due to the injury. home.headline: What to Know About Dolphins DT Zach Sieler's Mysterious Season-Ending Injury
home.blurb: To say this news came out of nowhere would be putting it mildly, considering Sieler played 42 snaps in the 19-9 loss against the Lions, only four fewer than he played against New England in Week 8. What is notable, however, is that on the very first play from scrimmage against Detroit, a 2-yard run by Jahmyr Gibbs, Sieler was sporting a black contraption around his right upper arm. Sieler was listed on the injury report last week with a shoulder injury and was a limited participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday before being full go Friday. Against the Lions, Sieler finished with one tackle, good for a 3-yard loss on a running play by Gibbs. While he didn't register a stat on the play, it was his initial pressure on Jared Goff that forced the quarterback out of the pocket and led to the third-down sack by Josh Uche in the first half. What to Know About Dolphins DT Zach Sieler's Mysterious Season-Ending Injury Skip to main content SI.COM There indeed was a major announcement regarding Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler on the day of the NFL trade deadline, but it had nothing to do with him being moved. Instead, the bombshell report involved a season-ending injury for the team captain. Sieler ruptured a biceps tendon against the Detroit Lions on Sunday and will undergo season-ending surgery, according to ESPN insider Adam Schefter, citing sources. Dolphins standout DT Zach Sieler ruptured his biceps and will undergo season-ending surgery, with a 5-6 month recovery expected, per sources. The injury happened on first play Sunday and he played the whole game with it. pic.twitter.com/N1ys0kzlkD The longest-tenured member of the roster, Sieler had been remarkably durable since joining the Dolphins as a waiver pick-up from the Baltimore Ravens in 2019, missing only two games over the past six seasons — that came in the 2024 season when he was poked in the eye during practice. There also was no Sieler injury reported in the press box, with the only one reported by the Dolphins being the quad injury to Will Kacmarek after he took a shot after catching a pass near the sideline. No injury being reported could be explained by Sieler not being tended to on the field or being away from the sideline at any point. The injury obviously quashed any notion of Sieler being traded before the 4 p.m. ET deadline Tuesday, even though reports indicated earlier the Dolphins had no intention of moving on from him regardless. Sieler has three more years left on the contract extension he signed in September 2025. He's got a cap number of $20.8 million next year with no guaranteed salary remaining, which would seem to make him a potential candidate for a contract restructure. The immediate impact is the Dolphins will be left without their best defensive lineman. home.headline: Dolphins QB Malik Willis to IR as groin injury worsens; Kyle McCord to start at QB
home.blurb: Dolphins standout Zach Sieler out for season due to injury Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content 🎉 November festivals & fun The groin injury for Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has worsened to the point that he will miss time on injured reserve. The Dolphins are placing Willis on IR, according to a league source Tuesday afternoon, which will sideline Willis a minimum of four games. Willis had been receiving treatment on a groin injury the past two weeks. He ran less than usual in the Nov. 1 loss to the New England Patriots (one attempt for 2 yards) but downplayed the effect of the ailing groin. After Sunday’s 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions, it was indisputable. He was visibly hindered by the groin and did not run with his usual swiftness as he escaped constant pressure from the Lions defensive front. At one point, he jogged to the sideline despite having open space in front of him for additional yardage. After the game, Willis admitted he felt the groin was tight. According to reports, an MRI showed the groin injury developed into a core muscle injury that requires rest. When Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley spoke Monday, Willis’ ailment had not yet been evaluated, so he had no update yet on the situation. Without Willis, the Dolphins are bound to start second-year quarterback Kyle McCord on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. McCord was acquired via trade with the Green Bay Packers ahead of the season, as Miami moved off of Quinn Ewers, the team’s backup quarterback to Willis in training camp, due to his performance in the preseason. home.headline: Dolphins Q&A: What has Malik Willis shown halfway through season; will Sieler play for Miami again?
home.blurb: My bigger concern is Willis’ durability. He’s been on the injury report the past two weeks with a groin problem, meaning he’s now spent four of the nine weeks of the season on the injury report with groin, toe and right thumb ailments. Willis is a 6-foot-1, 225-pound quarterback, which isn’t big, and he takes extra hits when he runs so you worry about him remaining available over a full season. It’s a shame that defensive tackle Zach Sieler is out for the season with an injury that he sustained on the first play of last Sunday’s 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions. It’s admirable he played the entire game. Sieler will be missed on the field and in the locker room. On the field his 24 tackles are tied for eighth on the team and his 2.0 sacks are third. Sieler is a key part of a run defense that is 16th against the run (111.8 yards allowed per game) so he’ll be missed on the field. picks.headline: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change?
picks.blurb: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change? Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints will take on the Cleveland Browns at noon Sunday. The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it.
