NFL Power Rankings Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup Caleb Yaccarino · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After two weeks without New Orleans Saints football, we are finally back. The Saints are also making their return to New Orleans, which may honestly be bad news for this team. The Saints have been unable to win a game at home this year, and some of their worst performances happened in New Orleans. For a team that has always valued the impact of playing at home, this is a really bad situation to be in, especially given how vocal fans can be. It also doesn't help that the pressure on the coaching staff to perform is palpable. The Saints also made some really important changes before this game. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, and they cut some players, including kicker Daniel Carlson and RB Kendre Miller. Each move made sense, and it is the first time we have seen real consequences from Kellen Moore's coaching staff. As I mentioned, the pressure is on this team, so we might as well try new things. For their opponent, it is a winnable game. The Cleveland Browns have been surprisingly one of the best teams in the NFL this season. They have had to make some crazy comebacks to make it happen, but QB Deshaun Watson is having a resurgence in his career. The defense is also playing really well, with the pass rush and pass defense standing out. But Watson is likely going to be out for this game. As of now, Watson has missed practice all week and is questionable for Sunday, so Shedeur Sanders will likely start for Cleveland. Although Sanders has not played yet this year, the Saints shouldn't overlook what the young QB can do. He had ups and downs throughout his rookie year, and if he is on point when facing the Saints' defense, it can be difficult to stop. The real worry for New Orleans is the Browns' defense. They have had run defense issues, so if the Saints defy all odds and fix the run game, that could be a way to win this game, but the rest of the defense will cause issues for the Saints. Now on to the prediction. Even with Watson likely being out, it's extremely difficult for me to choose the Saints. I do think it's going to be a close game, just not a victory for New Orleans. They need to prove the changes actually mattered first before I can believe something will change. For the score, I have the Browns winning 30-28.

home.headline: Decision Made on Saints QB Derek Carr Return From Retirement
home.blurb: Decision Made on Saints QB Derek Carr Return From Retirement There has been the suggestion, technically started on Monday Night Football, that the Minnesota Vikings should see if Drew Brees will come out of retirement to play quarterback up north. Carr has been floated a couple of times since then as a potential candidate to return from retirement. Carr himself has even made it sound like something he would consider. Florio's report suggests that nothing is coming with Carr, but it's interesting that Underhill at least seems to think Carr could still consider a return at some point. Unlock the latest Heavy on Saints news — direct to your inbox. If the New Orleans Saints had a nickel for every time that one of their retired quarterbacks was floated in a trade rumor on Tuesday ahead of the NFL trading deadline, they'd have two nickels. That's not a lot, but it's weird that it has happened twice. And the latest update came on Tuesday afternoon, involving Derek Carr. Carr retired surprisingly before the 2025 season when the Saints may not have really seen it coming. At the time, Carr was facing a long injury recovery, and he chose to step away from the game while he dealt with throwing shoulder struggles. That's not going to be happening now, though, based on the latest updates. First, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio posted this on X: “Per source, Vikings have not contacted the Saints about QB Derek Carr. Because he's on the Saints' reserve/retired list, a trade would be required.” Then, Saints beat writer Nick Underhill weighed in with this: “This feels like the kind of scenario where Carr would consider coming back. And this feels like the team that should be calling on him. I doubt it would cost a whole lot, either.” If Carr returned, his rights would technically belong to the Saints. He was still under contract when he retired, so he was placed on the New Orleans reserve/retired list. That means that if Carr comes back, he's essentially back on the Saints contract he was on before he stepped away. And so any Carr comeback would have to come with a trade to move him to a new team (or a release by New Orleans). Carr couldn't just sign freely elsewhere without the Saints first doing something. For now, though, it seems to be a moot point. Billy Heyen Billy Heyen is a Heavy contributor with focus on the NFL and MLB. His reporting work has also included extensive work for The Sporting News, the Sandusky Register and Rochester's Democrat & Chronicle. Adventures in sports writing have also led to in-person coverage of the Buffalo Sabres, Cleveland Guardians, U.S. men's national soccer team and a variety of minor league baseball stories. New York will be coming into the week with a record of 4-2-1 on the season, coming off a much-needed bye. The Giants are in full control of the NFC East right now , with the rest of the division underperforming this season. And New York has a chance to put on even more distance between them and a rival this week. New York will be traveling to take on the Philadelphia Eagles this week, offering them a chance to take down an NFC East rival. The Eagles have been a mess this season, with the team seeing all sorts of injuries taking place across the roster. Philadelphia will be coming into the game against the Giants with a record of 2-6 on the season, with them having lost six straight games. The Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the game, as he's been ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a scary blood clot problem. The Eagles will be starting backup Joe Milton under center, hoping to give the offense a spark this week. Milton is fairly inexperienced in the NFL, and the Giants will look to take advantage of the situation in front of them. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

away.headline: J.J. McCarthy injury update as Giants QB exits vs. Eagles
away.blurb: The Giants initially announced McCarthy was "questionable" to return to their Week 9 game against the Eagles before he returned to the game. The Giants have just two quarterbacks on their game-day roster, so Winston will be the last line of defense against the Eagles. Below is a look at New York's quarterback depth chart with Dart out for the season because of a knee injury. The New York Giants briefly lost quarterback J.J. McCarthy to an apparent injury in the third quarter of his second start with the team. McCarthy's injury occurred when he was scrambling to his left on a designed quarterback run. The 23-year-old quarterback was hit hard in the midsection by Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun at the end of his run, and he remained on the ground in pain following the play. McCarthy was able to get to the sideline but appeared to be in a lot of pain. He was captured by the broadcast trying to throw passes, but he collapsed to the ground and grabbed at his right side after attempting a throw. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. He was then taken into the blue medical tent for further evaluation following his brief throwing session. He was then seen jogging to the locker room, with athletic training staff in tow for the team. Here's what to know about McCarthy's injury. McCarthy officially returned to the game for the Giants after missing the remainder of their go-ahead touchdown drive because of a hip injury. McCarthy completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards and added 11 yards on three carries before being injured. He will look to add to that total after returning to the field. Jameis Winston is the Giants' backup quarterback. He opened the year as the backup to Jaxson Dart and made four starts before ceding the starting role to McCarthy in Week 7. Winston posted a 2-1-1 record while completing 57% of his passes for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 71 yards while leading the Giants to a touchdown on his lone drive replacing McCarthy against the Eagles. Haener, a 2024 fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints, has made one career start. home.blurb: The Giants initially announced McCarthy was "questionable" to return to their Week 9 game against the Eagles before he returned to the game. The Giants have just two quarterbacks on their game-day roster, so Winston will be the last line of defense against the Eagles. Below is a look at New York's quarterback depth chart with Dart out for the season because of a knee injury. The New York Giants briefly lost quarterback J.J. McCarthy to an apparent injury in the third quarter of his second start with the team. McCarthy's injury occurred when he was scrambling to his left on a designed quarterback run. The 23-year-old quarterback was hit hard in the midsection by Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun at the end of his run, and he remained on the ground in pain following the play. McCarthy was able to get to the sideline but appeared to be in a lot of pain. He was captured by the broadcast trying to throw passes, but he collapsed to the ground and grabbed at his right side after attempting a throw. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. He was then taken into the blue medical tent for further evaluation following his brief throwing session. He was then seen jogging to the locker room, with athletic training staff in tow for the team. Here's what to know about McCarthy's injury. McCarthy officially returned to the game for the Giants after missing the remainder of their go-ahead touchdown drive because of a hip injury. McCarthy completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards and added 11 yards on three carries before being injured. He will look to add to that total after returning to the field. Jameis Winston is the Giants' backup quarterback. He opened the year as the backup to Jaxson Dart and made four starts before ceding the starting role to McCarthy in Week 7. Winston posted a 2-1-1 record while completing 57% of his passes for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 71 yards while leading the Giants to a touchdown on his lone drive replacing McCarthy against the Eagles. home.headline: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game
home.blurb: There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle. If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night. NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Giants RB Cam Skattebo Doubtful for Eagles Game After Missing a Third Straight Practice Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game Skip to main content SI.COM New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice. Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago. At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.” Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans. Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury. If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game. "I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray). "So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll." While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia. Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring. Abdul Carter Remains Sidelined by Illness Lineback

Stuckey · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:01 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams (4-4) and Washington Commanders (2-4-1) meet today in NFL Week 9 action. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Rams are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Rams -4.5), with the over/under set at 47.5. Los Angeles is a -225 moneyline favorite while Washington is a +188 underdog. Let's get into my Rams vs Commanders predictions for today's NFC clash. Rams vs Commanders pick: Commanders Moneyline (+190) My Rams vs. Commanders best bet is Washington moneyline, with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Rams vs Commanders Odds Rams vs Commanders Spread : Rams -4.5 (-110), Commanders +4.5 (-110) Rams vs Commanders Over/Under : 47.5 (-120o / +100u) Rams vs Commanders Moneyline : Rams -225, Commanders +188 Rams vs Commanders Preview This handicap is entirely a bet against the health of Matthew Stafford . Stafford looked horrendous last week. He was seen icing his shoulder on the sideline, and the film backed up the injury concerns. He posted the lowest average depth of target (aDOT) of his entire career. The ball was fluttering out of his hand, floating downfield with hardly any zip — and if your quarterback cannot physically drive the football, you are in major trouble. To make matters worse, the Rams are still without Davante Adams on the outside, and their defense lost starting cornerback Jaylen Watson for the season. One major positive for the Rams on the injury front is that Myles Garrett is expected to play in this game. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has been sidelined since Week 1 after undergoing knee surgery. Commanders Preview The Commanders defense remains incredibly stout against the run, largely thanks to their Brian Flores-esque scheme. They blitz relentlessly, fill the interior gaps, and make life miserable for opposing running backs. Offensively, Jayden Daniels and company continue to move the ball with efficiency. Daniels can easily use his legs to extend plays, which will be vital against a Rams defensive front that will have both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. Rams vs Commanders Moneyline Prediction If the betting market is not properly accounting for Matthew Stafford operating at less than 100% with a compromised throwing shoulder, then the Commanders are very live underdogs in this spot. I'll take a flier on the Washington moneyline this week. picks.headline: Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13
picks.blurb: Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Yahoo Fantasy Forecast | NFL Trade Deadline Reactions TRENDING NFL trade deadline tracker Colts keep Taylor Vikings trade for Cousins Celtics better minus Brown? NFL Power Rankings Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Myles Garrett #95 celebrates with Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams after sack against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) (Getty Images) Myles Simmons · ProFootball Talk on NBC Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome back, Myles Garrett. The star edge rusher returned from a knee procedure and showed the difference he can make, racking up 3.0 sacks in the Rams' 20-13 victory over the Commanders on Sunday afternoon. Garrett's first sack also forced a fumble, as he poked the ball out from quarterback Jayden Daniels in the second quarter. That led to a field goal late in the half, which cut Washington's lead to 10-6 at halftime. Garrett then had two more in the fourth quarter, one of which came after he'd just been flagged for an offside penalty. While Garrett starred on defense, receiver Puka Nacua paced the offense with 14 catches for 150 yards with a touchdown. His 14 receptions are the third-most he's had in a single game in his career. He also had a pair of carries for 20 yards. The Commanders had a 10-6 lead at halftime from a 37-yard field goal and a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels to Van Jefferson. The Rams got two field goals from Brandon McManus for their six points. But the Rams were able to double up with a touchdown on their first drive of the second half. Blake Corum ran it in for a 1-yard score to cap an eight-play, 69-yard drive. And while a Matthew Stafford interception allowed the Commanders to tie the game at 13-13, Stanford then threw a touchdown to Nacua to put the Rams ahead for good. Washington had a chance to at least tie the game late, but time ran out on their last drive. Daniels finished the game 24-of-35 for 273 yards with a touchdown. He had four carries for 16 yards. Stafford finished 26-of-43 for 228 yards with a TD and a pick. At 5-4, the Rams are now above .500 for the first time this season and on a three-game winning streak. The team will be on the road to face division-rival Arizona next weekend before a Week 11 bye. The Commanders have fallen to 2-5-1. They won't have much time to think about their missed opportunities, as they'll face the Giants on Thursday night in Week 10.

NFL Power Rankings Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Landover got a feel-good Sunday night last week, when Washington scored 27 straight points in the 27-10 win over Philadelphia . The national picks aren't buying a second straight upset. Matthew Stafford's Los Angeles Rams arrive at Northwest Stadium as near-unanimous picks to beat Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders, and our staff went 4-0 for the Rams in this week's picks against the spread . When we added up the straight-up picks from ESPN, NFL.com, Sports Illustrated and CBS Sports' Pete Prisco, 18 of 19 took Los Angeles. The spread picks read differently. Six of the 14 analysts at CBS Sports and Bleacher Report who picked against the number have Washington covering a line that has sat between 4.5 and 5.5 points this week, and the nine analysts who gave a final score average out to a Rams win of 5.8 points, right on top of that number. ESPN and NFL.com go 8-0 for Los Angeles Nov 1, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders running back Austin Ekeler (30) runs against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Pamela Maldonado (24-17), Eric Moody (27-19) and Seth Walder (27-17) all took the Rams in ESPN's Week 9 game guide , and ESPN's Football Power Index gives Los Angeles a 72.2% chance to win. Walder's bold prediction belongs to Washington, though. He has rookie Antonio Williams catching at least six passes for a career high, which fits with Williams leading the receiver room and with Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown both ruled out for Sunday . All five NFL.com editors picked the Rams, from Bobby Kownack's 24-20 to Jeremy Bergman's 30-24. Bergman still expects a fight. "This one will be closer than most expect," he wrote in NFL.com's Week 9 picks . Mitch Goldich is Washington's lone believer Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs (3) scores a touchdown during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on Oct. 19, 2026.Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Nine of the 10 panelists in Sports Illustrated's straight-up picks took Los Angeles. Senior editor Mitch Goldich is the only national analyst we found picking the Commanders to win outright, and he made that call with Myles Garrett cleared for his first game since Week 1. With Laremy Tunsil out, Brandon Coleman draws Garrett at left tackle, and Dan Quinn didn't downplay the assignment. away.headline: NFL analyst is worried about Rams star Puka Nacua’s longevity after latest injuries
away.blurb: One NFL analyst expressed great concern about Los Angeles Rams star receiver Puka Nacua ’s long-term success in the league following his latest injury this season. Nacua shines as one of the best receivers in the NFL, giving Los Angeles a case for serious playoff contention. However, he suffered an MCL/PCL sprain as he will miss several weeks. NFL insider Marc Spears provided his thoughts on Nacua’s injury during his Monday appearance on NFL GameDay. He has concerns about the receiver’s longevity given his injury history. “If you think about how much he’s been hurt, and he’s been hurt because of his physicality in play. He’s not afraid to go across the middle, he seeks contact after he catches the football, he takes shots in games where you like, damn, is he even gonna get up from those shots? So I think more than anything right now with the Rams, because this is going to be your number one receiver. Davante was playing great, but Davante was brought in to complement Puka Nacua based on all of the things that he did in this offense,” Spears said. I don’t know how you change any of that, but I am concerned about Puka Nacua and the Los Angeles Rams and the longevity, and I don’t want to be cheated of a great player like him. Because if you think about, there’s a laundry list of injuries now that’s starting to mount up with Puka’s career, and it’s a direct reflection in how he plays, unfortunately.” Los Angeles has a 5-4 record this season, sitting at third place in the NFC West Division standings. away.headline: Rams Midweek Report: A Concerning Trend on Offense, Matthew Stafford's Elbow, and Trade Buzz
away.blurb: Through the first eight weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams’ offense has been productive but inconsistent, to say the least. The Rams rank fourth in yards per game and third in offensive success rate. However, after failing to score 20 points against the Arizona Cardinals before scoring 35 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams went three-and-out on their first five possessions last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. That was something that a Rams offense hadn’t done this century. There is certainly some context to that as Davante Adams and Puka Nacua have each missed games. Terrance Ferguson has also been out since Week 3. At the same time, the Rams haven’t pushed the ball down the field very often. The Rams have found success out of 13 personnel, but at some point the Rams need to be able to throw the ball. It’s easy to run against inferior teams when the game script is in your favor. However, when that goes south against a true contender, they need to be able to have confidence in their passing game. The eventual return of Ferguson and Adams will help, but is it enough? Two of Matthew Stafford’s 10 lowest single-game averages in intended air yards per attempt have come this season. He has had four straight games averaging under six intended air yards per pass attempt. Over the last four weeks, Stafford has an average depth of target of 5.5 yards, ranking 25 out of 27 quarterbacks. One of the big stories coming out of Sunday’s game was Matthew Stafford being seen leaving the locker room with a bag of ice around his arm. Coincidentally, after not showing up on the injury report all season, Stafford was listed with a right elbow injury this week. Despite Stafford saying he’s fine, this isn’t something to completely sweep under the rug either. It’s well known that Stafford is one of the toughest quarterbacks in the NFL. home.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested
away.blurb: The Broncos play the Carolina Panthers in Week 9, and it's the team's final game before the Week 10 bye, which comes at a perfect time. The team's final injury report does test the depth of this defense but also sees the return of a key rotational player on offense. All of Dondrea Tillman, Talanoa Hufanga, Kris Abrams-Draine, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike are either out or questionable in Week 9: Even with Bryant being listed as questionable, he'll play in Week 9: Hufanga's return will be the key to watch, and if you look at Denver's injury report from Week 8, there seems to be a good chance that the starting safety returns: In this practice week, Hufanga went DNP, Limited, and Limited and is listed as questionable. Just last week, the Broncos saw both Zach Allen and Jaylen Waddle have the exact same practice week, and both were also listed as questionable. Both played, so there is reason to believe that the Broncos took Hufanga's practice statuses this week with the same idea in mind. It does flat-out stink that the Broncos are going to still be down a starting safety with a likely Hufanga return. Jones hurt his hamstring during the win over Kansas City in Week 8 and did not practice all week. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested . For the most part, the Denver Broncos have stayed healthy this year, but they have dealt with a good bit of injuries to primary depth, rotational players. We have already seen Jonah Coleman spent time on IR. Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey are both on IR, along with Jonah Elliss. The team has also seen Pat Bryant be placed on IR. Patrick Surtain II just recently missed time as well. All in all, Denver is certainly no strangers to injuries this year, but, for the most part, the primary starters are healthy and in a good spot. Denver Broncos final injury report for Week 9 against the Panthers In an ideal world, both Tillman and Hufanga suit up. If not, the depth of this defense is going to be tested big-time. The offense is clearly much healthier, as every one of the primary starters are healthy enough to play. I guess if we had to 'pick' one side to be hurt more, it would be the defense given how good this unit has been for years now, but that doesn't make this week's report any less shaky. The Broncos getting a win in Week 9. moving to 7-2, and having two weeks off would be the absolute best-case scenario. Denver's bye would allow every banged-up player to get healthier, and it would also present a perfect opportunity for the team to add a player or two at the NFL Trade Deadline and get them up to speed with the bye. Even in a loss, the Broncos sitting at 6-3 would still position themselves well down the stretch, especially with the ease of the remaining schedule. Wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle) is also listed as questionable, but he was listed as a full participant for the third consecutive day. Bryant, who returned to practice this week, is eligible to make his return against the Panthers if the team activates him from injured reserve. Bryant last played in Week 4 against the San Francisco 49ers. Outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hip) was added to the team's practice report on Friday as a full participant. He is also questionable for the game. Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) and defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) were all ruled out after they did not practice for a third consecutive day. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

It’s not who you play but when you play them. The Green Bay Packers will face the New England Patriots on Sunday. It’s a measuring-stick game for the Packers, who believe they are Super Bowl contenders. The Patriots played in the Super Bowl last year and believe they have the goods to take the next step. With a top-tier quarterback and coach and a strong defense, they will be a formidable challenge. The Patriots, however, will play without their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Their premier tight end, Hunter Henry, is questionable with a foot injury that held him out of practice to start the week. Their starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu, are on injured reserve. So is their top pass rusher, Harold Landry. Can the Packers take advantage of the “when you play them” part of that adage? Here are our weekly game predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Patriots Prediction The Packers have had some good fortune this season. They faced the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield and the Bears without Caleb Williams. They will have more good fortune against the Patriots. While Drake Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up, will be the starting quarterback, he’s going to be playing with an incredibly shorthanded group of receivers. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are not the same as A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Good quarterbacks can make it work with whoever, so this won’t be a layup victory for Jonathan Gannon’s defense. However, New England’s pass protection has been leaky, with Maye facing the fourth-highest pressure rate in the league. Can the Patriots’ receivers get open before the Packers’ pass rush arrives on the scene? Added together, the game has been put on a silver platter for Green Bay’s defense to be the most powerful unit on the field. On the other side of the ball, it’s going to be a challenging day for Jordan Love, as well. The Packers, of course, can’t run the football, and it’s having an impact on the passing game with the play-action attack having become irrelevant . If the Packers can’t run the ball – and what reason is there to believe they will? – they’re going to have to deal with the teeth of the Patriots’ strong pass rush, which ranks fifth in sack percentage. Elijah Ponder – the best pass rusher that nobody has ever heard of – is seventh in the league with six sacks. With 3.5 sacks, Christian Barmore powers the interior rush. “He’s a really good player,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of Ponder, an undrafted free agent last year. “To be truthful, I hadn’t heard a whole lot about him until I started watching the tape and I’m like who is this guy? What’s his story? How do we not know about him? Everybody knows about him now. When you look at their edges, all three of those guys that are really doing the bulk of the work are really good players, and you couple that with the interior guys, it’s a really formidable front.” That could mean limited time for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat the premier cornerback duo of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. “Really good DBs,” Love said. “I think they do a lot of things very well. I think as anything, it’s a challenge for me, for the receivers on the outside to be able to go see how good we can be and how good we can attack them and make plays against them. I think they do a really good job. I think Gonzalez is definitely one of the best in the league and he makes plays. I feel like for us, it’s a fun test.” Ultimately, I’m taking the Packers, who are 3-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . Both quarterbacks are really good, but I’ll take Watson and Golden vs. Gonzalez and Davis over Hollins and Douglas vs. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. In a close game, the Packers will fail to run out the clock but the defense will save the day. And they’ll need it, with the Bears and Lions favored to win their games against the Buccaneers and Dolphins, respectively, while the first-place Vikings are underdogs against Buffalo. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 20. Bill’s Record: 6-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Patriots Prediction Everything outside of the field favors New England in this game with the return of Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady, which has been discussed all week. The reality on the field, however, is that the Packers have more healthy players than the Patriots do. The Patriots are missing their top two receivers and their starting tight end is going to be hobbled, at minimum, if he can play. Drake Maye and Jordon Love are both being asked to carry a heavy load, but Love has a better supporting cast around him. In addition, Jonathan Gannon should be able to create enough confusion for Maye to make a couple of mistakes that swing the game in the Packers’ favor. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 17. Jacob’s Record: 5-3. picks.blurb: These Are the Three Factors Packers Must Take Advantage of to Beat Patriots Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have their eyes on the Super Bowl. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough in what is truly a measuring-stick game for the Packers. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. In front of a national audience with Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game, I don't see how this week ends in a loss. What it will take is Maye slinging it just like he's done the last few games and use his legs to extend some plays — as well as not letting Green Bay's rushing attack with Josh Jacobs find its footing. Tom Brady will be in the booth for his former team's Week 9 matchup, and the action at Gillette Stadium promises plenty of drama on the field too as the New England Patriots host the Green Bay Packers. With New England laying 3. 5 points as home favorites and the total set at 44. 5 points, my top Packers vs. Patriots predictions and NFL picks back Green Bay's relentless pass defense to steal the spotlight, keeping this affair close enough for the road underdogs to cover. It all gets started at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. TOP PICK Packers vs Patriots prediction today: Packers +3.5 I'm locking in the Green Bay Packers +3.5, down to +2.5 , because they have better net early-down EPA per play and a higher quarterback-pressure rate differential than the New England Patriots , and I like this matchup for Green Bay's defense. According to RBSDM.com, the Packers rank third in weighted defensive EPA per dropback . Drake Maye struggled against the Seahawks (fifth), Steelers (sixth), and Jaguars (fourth), completing just 63.8% of his passes with one touchdown and six interceptions. Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon also gets extra prep time for a New England offense without wide receiver A.J. Brown and possibly without Mack Hollins and tight end Hunter Henry . Green Bay limits explosives, forcing Maye to work the ball methodically downfield, where we've already seen him make costly mistakes. Packers vs Patriots combo I expect Green Bay to dictate the terms defensively, but that doesn't mean the Packers need to win outright for me to cash. New England can move the chains without producing explosive plays, which helps running back Rhamondre Stevenson pile up receiving yards while keeping the game within one possession. Meanwhile, Green Bay doesn't need a monster offensive performance, either. One well-executed red-zone possession could be enough for tight end Tucker Kraft to find pay dirt. The beauty of this angle is that I don't need either quarterback to light up the scoreboard . In fact, a relatively ugly, low-scoring game could work perfectly fine for all three legs. John Lanfranca · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 8:07 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (5-3) take on the New England Patriots (5-3) today in NFL Week 9 action. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Patriots are 3-point favorites on the spread (Patriots -3), with the over/under set at 44.5 (-112o / -108u). The Patriots are -170 favorites on the moneyline and the Packers are +142 underdogs. Let's get into my Packers vs Patriots Week 9 prediction . Packers vs Patriots pick: Packers +3 (-110) My Packers vs Patriots best bet is on Green Bay to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Packers vs Patriots Odds Packers vs Patriots Spread : Packers +3 (-105), Patriots -3 (-115) Packers vs Patriots Over/Under : 44.5 (-112o / -108u) Packers vs Patriots Moneyline : Packers +142, Patriots -170 Packers vs Patriots Week 9 Preview The Packers under head coach Matt LaFleur have been an excellent team to back when they are priced as underdogs. LaFleur has covered 65.1% of all games when his team is catching points, and I believe this is another very good spot for Green Bay to potentially steal a victory. The narrative surrounding the Packers offense has to do with their lack of pass protection, as every mention of their future outlook as a Super Bowl contender is usually followed by a comment regarding their offensive line issues. Jordan Love is navigating those issues quite well, as it may be surprising to some that he has just a 32% pressure rate on all of his dropbacks. Only seven quarterbacks with 200 or more dropbacks have faced pressure less often than Love this season. We already know Green Bay struggles to run the football effectively, and that data point is completely baked into the line here. Sure, most of the offensive success for this team is squarely on the shoulders of Love, but that is something I am completely comfortable with against a Patriots team that ranks 26th in quick pressure percentage. Quick pressures occur within 2.5 seconds of the snap, and it is not something I am concerned about happening regularly in this matchup. If there is a signal caller who will be under constant duress in this game, it is likely to be Drake Maye . Maye has regained his MVP-level play from a season ago, but protection issues that plagued this team in the playoffs remain. The 44% pressure rate allowed by the New England offensive line is the highest rate league-wide. The Packers are generating pressure at the 12th-highest rate, but more importantly, they are converting those pressures into sacks. Green Bay has 22 sacks on the season, the sixth-most in the NFL. While the Packers' pass rush is undoubtedly above average, it has been the coverage in the secondary that has been this defense's biggest strength. Green Bay allows just 6.2 yards per pass attempt (fifth-best) while also ranking among the top five pass defenses in expected points added (EPA) per pass against. During Maye's hot streak, he has been doing his best work when throwing down the field. Maye leads the league in touchdown passes of 20 or more yards downfield this season, in addition to being efficient in the intermediate areas of the field. Over the past five weeks, Maye has completed 67% of his throws that have traveled more than 10 yards past the line of scrimmage. However, it is worth noting he has not played the most difficult slate of defenses during that stretch. The Packers are a completely different animal defensively than the teams Maye has shredded in recent weeks. During that same span of five games, Green Bay is second in the league in defensive EPA. The Packers specialize in limiting explosive plays — allowing the third-fewest of any defense in football. On throws 10 or more yards downfield, the Packers have allowed opposing quarterbacks to complete just 44% of their passes, generating seven interceptions while allowing just two touchdowns. The Patriots are not equipped to pressure Love as often as they need to, but the Packers do possess the tools to halt numerous New England possessions with their sticky coverage and timely pass rush led by Devonte Wyatt and Lukas Van Ness . Packers vs Patriots Spread Prediction, Betting Analysis Jordan Love and Drake Maye are in good form — both rank inside the top 12 of qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted net yards per attempt, have passer ratings that exceed 105.0 when kept clean and boast identical big-time throw rates. Let's call it a wash at quarterback. The team protecting their passer more cleanly also happens to be the team with the decided advantage defensively. Getting three points with the Packers in this spot is a tremendous value. Add in Matt LaFleur's success rate at covering the number as an underdog during his tenure as Packers head coach, and this may be one of my strongest positions of the NFL season thus far. NFL Power Rankings Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

NFL Power Rankings (USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect) Andrew Kulha · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are back at it after what feels like forever. It feels like they're coming off a bye heading into Week 9's matchup with the New England Patriots. And to be fair, it was a mini-bye. The Packers last played on October 29 on Thursday Night Football. By the time you're reading this, that was 10 days ago. Double-digit days is a long time to go without playing football in the NFL. For the Packers, it was a chance to re-set after a 5-3 start, though. Frankly, it was a much-needed re-set, and hopefully it will have done this team well. There's still extremely injured and maddeningly inconsistent on this side of the mini-bye, but Jordan Love is playing like a potential MVP candidate , Jonathan Gannon's defense looks really good and oh...Micah Parsons is getting back to practice. That's right, the multi-time All-Pro is getting back to it, though he's not making any promises regarding his level of play. He's also likely not to be activated until the night before Thanksgiving, so he wont' play a role in this one. That is a shame, because the Packers are on the road against one of the better teams in the AFC in the 5-3 Patriots. Here's everything (else) you need to know about this game. Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, MA) 3:25 PM Lambeau Time Packers Injury Report: Questionable: Chris Brooks (Ankle), MarShawn Lloyd (Knee), Keisean Nixon (Groin), Out: Zaire Franklin (Shin), Travis Glover (Knee), Micah Parsons (Knee), Sean Rhyan (Ankle), Josh Whyle (Concussion) Patriots Injury Report: Questionable: Hunter Henry (Foot), Kevin Byard (Chest), Carlton Davis III (Neck), Morgan Moses (Foot), Brenden Schooler (Hamstring), Greg Van Roten (Hamstring), Out: A.J. Brown (Ankle/Knee), TreVeyon Henderson (Illness), Betting Odds: Packers +3.5, per DraftKings Key Matchup: Brandon Cisse vs. DeMario Douglas A.J. Brown was supposed to be a huge addition this offseason for the Patriots, but he's appeared in just three games this season due to injury. Tight end Hunter Henry is hopeful that he'll play, but he was limited in practice on Friday and did not practice earlier in the week. Running back TreVeyon Henderson is scarily dealing with neurological symptoms . With all that firepower hampered, the Patriots are relaying on former 2023 sixth-round pick DeMario Douglas to fuel their offense. Douglas is having the best season of his career so far, with 26 catches for 332 yards and four touchdowns, but he's not the type of player the Pack will lose sleep game planning against. In the meantime, Packers' rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse was the NFL's defensive rookie of the month after recording 21 tackles, seven passes defended, one interception and one sack in October. Cisse appears to be a rising star, and he should be able to neutralize Douglas when asked to go one-on-one with the former Liberty wideout. Key Quote: Legendary NFL quarterback Tom Brady on Jordan Love "He's throwing the ball out of the pocket, in the pocket, down the field, he's seeing things so well," Brady said . "Coach LaFleur has a ton of confidence in him. When the coordinator and head coach have so much confidence in the quarterback, he's just gonna keep throwing it out there. … Jordan Love is playing exceptional football. This is the best of his career." Packers 20, Patriots 17

away.headline: Packers make 2 updates to week 9 injury report: Keisean Nixon DNP
away.blurb: Nixon did not practice on Thursday while dealing with a groin injury. He was listed as limited on Wednesday. The veteran has not missed a game since signing with the Packers before the 2022 season, but he might need to practice Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the New England Patriots. Lloyd, who suffered through two injury-plagued seasons to start his NFL career, has his first injury of 2026: a knee injury. He was limited on Thursday. It's possible the Packers could return Chris Brooks this week, providing depth at running back if Lloyd can't go. Micah Parsons practiced in a limited capacity for the second straight day after returning on Wednesday. The Packers were in pads on Thursday. Parsons is not expected to play until Week 12 at the earliest. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), EDGE Micah Parsons (knee), WR Christian Watson (rib), RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee) Note: Brooks is designated to return from injured reserve; Parsons is on the PUP list. Both opened their 21-day practice windows on Wednesday. Limited participation: S Kevin Byard III (chest), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), WR Mack Hollins (calf), OLB Gabe Jacas (knee), LB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee), T Morgan Moses (foot), OL Greg Van Roten (hamstring), S Brenden Schooler (hamstring) This article originally appeared on Packers Wire: Packers make 2 updates to Week 9 injury report: Keisean Nixon DNP The Green Bay Packers made two adjustments to the Week 9 injury report on Thursday: cornerback Keisean Nixon was downgraded and running back MarShawn Lloyd was added. In addition to Nixon, the Packers did not have Zaire Franklin, Sean Rhyan, Travis Glover or Josh Whyle at Thursday's practice. All five are in danger of not playing against the Patriots. The Patriots made three changes: defensive lineman Christian Barmore practiced after missing Wednesday with an illness, while the team added cornerback Marcus Jones (foot) and safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) to the injury report with new injuries. Receiver A.J. Brown didn't practice for the second straight day, so it's possible the Packers will be down a starting corner while the Patriots will be down two starting receivers (including former Packer Romeo Doubs, who is on injured reserve). The Packers and Patriots will have final practices on Friday before issuing status designations on the final injury report. away.headline: Patriots vs. Packers takeaways: Jordan Love, Christian Watson lead dominant Green Bay performance
away.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Jordan Love (372 yards passing and four total touchdowns), Christian Watson (171 yards receiving and a touchdown) and Matthew Golden (164 yards receiving and a touchdown) tore up the Patriots' secondary all day long. Much of Golden's damage came against Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, the NFL's highest-paid cornerback. Green Bay's defense also shined with four turnovers forced-- three interceptions of Drake Maye and a forced fumble out of Rhamondre Stevenson's hands. Yes, the Packers aren't without warts, but they have what it takes to win the NFC North. The division-leading Minnesota Vikings (6-1) do have the league's best defense across numerous metrics, but the Packers lead the NFL with 19 takeaways. Against Maye on Sunday, Green Bay produced 11 unblocked pressures, the second most in a game this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The Packers now lead the NFL with 43 unblocked pressures, the most in the NFL, and that's without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. Parsons is set to return in a couple weeks against the Los Angeles Rams. Green Bay pressured Maye on 51.2% of his dropbacks on Sunday, the highest pressure rate of his career in the regular season. The Packers nearly matched the 52.8% pressures rate the Seahawks hit against him in the Super Bowl last season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Minnesota also has a big quarterback issue with Kyler Murray not fitting into coach Kevin O'Connell's scheme through the first half of the season. Their record could also begin to level out as they play the NFL's toughest schedule from Weeks 8-11. The Detroit Lions needed a buzzer-beater field goal and questionable calls to defeat Green Bay in Detroit in Week 20-17 in Week 7. They face the Packers again in Week 18. Green Bay already beat the Chicago Bears 31-7 in Week 5, and even though Chicago was without Caleb Williams that day, the Bears were the betting favorites at Lambeau Field that day. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love found wide receiver Savion Williams, a 2025 third-round pick out of TCU, in the back left corner of the end zone for the 10-yard touchdown on third down. He is now up to 270 yards passing and 2 two passing touchdowns on 16 of 21 passing, in addition to a 13-yard rushing touchdown, one drive into the second half. The Packers are back up 17, 31-14, with 10:51 left in the third quarter. The New England Patriots needed just four plays to travel 64 yards down the field for a touchdown. All 64 yards came from Drake Maye's right arm as he completed throws of 9 yards, 28 yards, 19 yards and 8 eight yards. The last throw was a floater of a touchdown pass from eight yards out to wide receiver Efton Chism. New England trails by 10, 24-14, with 2:42 left in the first half. away.blurb: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday Emma Pravecek, packers.com CB Keisean Nixon GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) as questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. New England has ruled out receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and listed seven question: tight end Hunter Henry (foot), cornerback Carlton Davis (neck), safety Kevin Byard (chest), receiver Mack Hollins (calf/injured reserve), tackle Morgan Moses (foot), safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring/IR). The Patriots didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder), cornerback Marcus Jones (foot), defensive tackle Christian Barmore (illness), and linebackers Gabe Jacas (knee) and Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee). ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window **Designated for Return from Reserve List/Injured CB Keisean Nixon has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's game against the Panthers news Packers list four questionable, rule out three vs. Panthers | Week 8 Injury Report WR Matthew Golden, DT Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night news Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Wes Hodkiewicz packers.c

home.headline: Patriots Face Running Back Crisis Before Munich After Rhamondre Stevenson Injury
home.blurb: Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to miss multiple weeks with an injury involving the plantaris tendon behind his knee, according to reports attributed to NFL Network's Ian Rapopor t and ESPN's Adam Schefter. The injury occurred during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers, when Stevenson exited in the second half and did not return. The reported absence is particularly concerning because TreVeyon Henderson has also been unavailable. That leaves the Patriots potentially relying on two less-experienced options during a difficult stretch of their schedule. Corey Kiner appears positioned for an expanded role if Stevenson and Henderson remain unavailable. Lan Larison is another option, particularly in passing situations. New England also has Terrell Jennings available on its practice squad if additional depth becomes necessary. New England's next practice reports should clarify which backs are available. For now, a position that appeared reasonably deep earlier in the season has become one of the team's biggest concerns heading to Germany. The New England Patriots are preparing for their first regular-season game in Munich, but their backfield could look dramatically different when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Stevenson Has Been More Than A Runner Stevenson has carried the ball 102 times for 399 yards and two touchdowns this season, but his contributions extend beyond rushing production. He also has 26 receptions for 258 yards and two receiving touchdowns, providing Drake Maye with a dependable outlet in the passing game. Stevenson has handled approximately 65% of New England's offensive snaps, reflecting the importance of his role in multiple personnel packages. His pass protection is another element the Patriots must replace. Losing a running back who understands blitz pickups can affect the entire offense, particularly when the offensive line is already dealing with injuries. Corey Kiner Could Receive His Biggest Opportunity Kiner has rushed for 244 yards and a touchdown on 50 carries, averaging 4.9 yards per attempt. Those numbers suggest he can provide productive rushing plays, although a larger workload would test his consistency and ability to handle different assignments. MORE : Tom Brady Gives Blunt Assessment of Patriots Midway Through Season The Patriots must prepare for Detroit while managing international travel and a short window to reorganize their backfield. Maye threw three interceptions against Green Bay, making offensive balance especially important as New England attempts to rebound. A dependable rushing attack could reduce the pressure on its quarterback, but that task becomes more difficult without Stevenson. home.headline: Patriots final Week 9 injury report: Good news, bad news
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Star wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have already been ruled out for the game. The Patriots might also be missing tight end Hunter Henry, who is still battling the foot injury he suffered in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten both returned from injured reserve this week to practice. They are officially listed as questionable to play against the Packers. The New England Patriots will once again be shorthanded on the offensive side of the ball when hosting the Green Bay Packers for a visit on Sunday. But it isn't all bad news for the Patriots. Hollins has been one of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable downfield targets, and Van Roten was the top replacement at right guard behind Mike Onwenu. Those returns would be a huge lift to a Patriots offense that needs all of the help it can get. home.headline: A.J. Brown Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Return Timeline Amid Patriots' 'Optimistic' Outlook
home.blurb: The quick turnaround between the games may have put additional stress on Brown's knee, but the Patriots are "optimistic" he could return after the team's Week 11 bye, according to Pelissero. Bleacher Report • 2h Vikings WR Calls Out Haters 😶 New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss his second consecutive game due to a knee injury that has hampered him throughout his career, but the team isn't down on his prospects, insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, but the results have been underwhelming through the first half of the season. Brown suffered an ankle injury during the team's regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. Lamar's Message to Ravens 🎙️ The 29-year-old returned from a stint on the injured reserve list in Week 6, and he played four days later when the Patriots faced the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. Then, Brown popped up on the injury report with a knee issue. The Los Angeles Rams were also interested in trading for Brown during the offseason, but they were reportedly scared off by the medical concerns with his knee, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported. New England head coach Mike Vrabel, who drafted Brown during his time as head coach of the Tennessee Titans, was evidently more comfortable with the medical evaluations. Brown has only caught passes in each of the three games he played in this season, bringing his tally up to nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns. There was belief that the eight-year veteran would be a great fit as a vertical threat for quarterback Drake Maye, who has been one of the best deep-ball passers in the league. That hasn't proven to be the case: Brown is only averaging 8.3 yards per catch — significantly down from his career average of 15.3 yards per reception.
