home.headline: Patriots vs. Packers takeaways: Jordan Love, Christian Watson lead dominant Green Bay performance
home.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Jordan Love (372 yards passing and four total touchdowns), Christian Watson (171 yards receiving and a touchdown) and Matthew Golden (164 yards receiving and a touchdown) tore up the Patriots' secondary all day long. Much of Golden's damage came against Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, the NFL's highest-paid cornerback. Green Bay's defense also shined with four turnovers forced-- three interceptions of Drake Maye and a forced fumble out of Rhamondre Stevenson's hands. Yes, the Packers aren't without warts, but they have what it takes to win the NFC North. The division-leading Minnesota Vikings (6-1) do have the league's best defense across numerous metrics, but the Packers lead the NFL with 19 takeaways. Against Maye on Sunday, Green Bay produced 11 unblocked pressures, the second most in a game this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The Packers now lead the NFL with 43 unblocked pressures, the most in the NFL, and that's without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. Parsons is set to return in a couple weeks against the Los Angeles Rams. Green Bay pressured Maye on 51.2% of his dropbacks on Sunday, the highest pressure rate of his career in the regular season. The Packers nearly matched the 52.8% pressures rate the Seahawks hit against him in the Super Bowl last season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Minnesota also has a big quarterback issue with Kyler Murray not fitting into coach Kevin O'Connell's scheme through the first half of the season. Their record could also begin to level out as they play the NFL's toughest schedule from Weeks 8-11. The Detroit Lions needed a buzzer-beater field goal and questionable calls to defeat Green Bay in Detroit in Week 20-17 in Week 7. They face the Packers again in Week 18. Green Bay already beat the Chicago Bears 31-7 in Week 5, and even though Chicago was without Caleb Williams that day, the Bears were the betting favorites at Lambeau Field that day. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love found wide receiver Savion Williams, a 2025 third-round pick out of TCU, in the back left corner of the end zone for the 10-yard touchdown on third down. He is now up to 270 yards passing and 2 two passing touchdowns on 16 of 21 passing, in addition to a 13-yard rushing touchdown, one drive into the second half. The Packers are back up 17, 31-14, with 10:51 left in the third quarter. The New England Patriots needed just four plays to travel 64 yards down the field for a touchdown. All 64 yards came from Drake Maye's right arm as he completed throws of 9 yards, 28 yards, 19 yards and 8 eight yards. The last throw was a floater of a touchdown pass from eight yards out to wide receiver Efton Chism. New England trails by 10, 24-14, with 2:42 left in the first half. Predicting the Raiders' Week 9 Moves In their Week 8 matchup against the Jets, Las Vegas made several notable changes to their starting lineup that proved fruitful. After struggling to find competent play at the right guard position between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, the Raiders turned to rookie Trey Zuhn. The Jets are not known for being a stout defense, but they are serviceable and gave Las Vegas fits for the entire first half, holding the Raiders to 97 total yards. Still, Zuhn looked like he may be the Raiders' best option at right guard for the rest of the season. Sunday's matchup against the 49ers will be much more telling, as San Francisco's defense is much more of a challenge than New York's. It will be interesting to see how Zuhn does at guard against one of the toughest teams the Raiders will face this season. He wants to get better at each and every single thing he does, whether it’s fitting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. It’s all the little fundamental things that we talk about. It’s stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that’ll allow him to become a more successful player,” Janocko said earlier this week. “Running the ball is a full team thing. The greatest thing about football in general is that it’s 11 as one on every single play. So, it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful." Cornerback Darien Porter returned to practice this week after playing only one play against the New York Jets last Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable heading into Week 9. However, speed is arguably Porter's greatest asset on the field, and he is dealing with a groin injury. A groin injury can linger. Despite being listed as questionable, Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard may decide not to risk damage to Porter's long-term health in a game where they already face an uphill battle. Las Vegas faced a similar decision earlier this season, when they could have rested running back Ashton Jeanty against a New England Patriots team that was missing more than five players before their matchup ended. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." Samuel and Evans are not expected to return Sunday, but the 49ers should get Demarcus Robinson back. NFL Power Rankings ESPN Analysts Give Their Picks for Week 9’s 49ers Versus Raiders Matchup Robert Marvi · Athlon Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their bye week, the San Francisco 49ers will take the field at Levi's Stadium on Sunday to take on the Las Vegas Raiders. With a 6-1 record, they will look to get back in the win column after losing their previous game on Oct. 25 to the Atlanta Falcons. The Raiders may have a mediocre 4-4 record and be struggling mightily on defense, but they do have the ability to give San Francisco some issues. That is especially true when one considers that San Francisco will be without wide receivers Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis), Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (meniscus). On the other hand, the Niners will welcome back defensive end Nick Bosa and wideout Demarcus Robinson for this game. Both men last played in Week 2 — Bosa had been out with a calf injury, and Robinson had been dealing with a high ankle sprain. Sunday's game will also mark the return of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, who was acquired in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts last week and hasn't played for the Niners since Super Bowl LIV. ESPN analysts Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody and Seth Walder gave their picks for the Niners vs. Raiders contest, and they were unanimous. The picks are in Maldonado picked the 49ers to win by a final score of 24-20. Moody went with the Niners by a score of 34-20 and Walder chose the Niners to win 29-23. One big negative for the Raiders is the fact that they're 31st in points allowed. While they have been able to force turnovers and have one of the NFL's best edge rushers in Maxx Crosby, they just haven't been able to stop opponents. Last week against the struggling New York Jets, they gave up 33 points and 439 yards of total offense. Their run defense has been particularly bad — they rank 31st in rushing yards given up and last in yards per carry allowed. This means the 49ers need to run, run and run some more. They have limited running back Christian McCaffrey's touches to keep him fresh, and given how short-handed they will be at wide receiver, perhaps this would be a nice time to increase his usage a bit. After this weekend, the Niners will visit the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday before meeting the Minnesota Vikings, who are currently 6-1, on Nov. 22 in Mexico City. away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

home.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. The Bears are 6.5-point favorites over the Buccaneers on the spread, with the over/under set at 47.5 total points. That may sound familiar because the Bears will be playing in primetime for the third straight week. That's pretty uncommon. For what it's worth, since 2003, teams playing their third consecutive primetime have gone 16-20 ATS. The past two victories have come against last year's Super Bowl participants with their most recent coming against Seattle with extra time to prepare. This situation is a little trickier since the Bears will be traveling back from Seattle on a short week, which can only be a positive for Tampa. The less time you give Ben Johnson to prepare for an opponent, the better, if you're that opponent. The Bucs have won two straight games in blowout fashion to get right back in the thick of the NFC South race. They've done so despite Baker Mayfield only completing seven total passes, including a grand total of zero last week in a monsoon against Atlanta. The Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass. That does make this handicap a little trickier since we really don't know if his previous thumb injury will be an issue when he has to throw more frequently, which he certainly will need to do tonight. Tampa has ridden its running game, spearheaded by Bucky Irving, and defense during its recent surge. Coming into this week, the Bucs ranked first overall in Defensive DVOA with no glaring holes in their analytical profile. In fact, they actually rank in the top-2 in both drop back and rushing EPA. Todd Bowles has this unit playing at an elite level at the moment, which will create a strength on strength matchup when the Bears have the ball. Chicago Bears Betting Preview There's not much more you can say about the Bears offense at the moment. You could argue it's the best in the NFL with a healthy Caleb Williams , who has seemingly taken a massive leap in the second year of Ben Johnson's offense. He's playing within the structure of the scheme, while also still sprinkling in those off-script explosive plays when things break down. Throw in a dominant ground game and this offense has juggernaut potential. The Chicago defense does have some holes. After all, the Bears are only one of two teams that have allowed six or more yards per play (along with the Raiders ). However, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen does seemingly have a good feel for this group and has been dialing up pressures at all the right times. Plus, this unit should continue to trend up following the addition of Jeffery Simmons and a now healthy Kyler Gordon , who Allen will blitz off the edge to generate some of that aforementioned pressure. It's never going to be an elite defense and there is likely some harsh third-down regression looming on the horizon. Chicago leads the NFL on those late downs by a wide margin at an insane 23.75%. Only one other team in the league has allowed a sub-30% and it's Minnesota at 29.75%. However, as long as Chicago's offense stays heathy and Ben Johnson is on the sidelines, it doesn't need its defense to be elite. Just not a total disaster and this is a true Super Bowl contender. Buccaneers vs Bears Prediction, Betting Analysis I like the Bucs here at +6 or better. I mentioned that potential third-down regression, but I also believe the Bucs will have success on the ground here in a game that might not have a ton of possessions, which makes the road pup a bit more intriguing. I have to imagine it's tough to get up emotionally for three straight primetime games, especially on a short week with travel after beating last year's conference winners. I wouldn't be totally surprised if the Bears were just a tad flat or off in the beginning parts of this game. While I don't think Tampa's defense can completely shut down Chicago's offense, the Buccaneers are playing as well as anybody in the league on that side of the ball at the moment. Even if I adjust for schedule, I have the Bucs rated as a top-3 defense this season — and in order to have a prayer against a Ben Johnson offense, you have to be stout against the run. Tampa has certainly fit that profile for years under Bowles and does so once again this season (second in rush DVOA). I'm selling high on the Bears and taking the six points with Baker and the boys. NFL Power Rankings Prediction For Buccaneers' Sunday Night Showdown With the Chicago Bears (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have shown everyone what they are capable of over the last two games. The Bucs have beaten the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons , a pair of NFC South rivals, by a combined score of 59-13 in the last two weeks to pull within a half-game of first place in the division. Now they must show they are capable of beating one of the NFL's top teams when they go on the road to take on the 6-2 Chicago Bears on Sunday night. The Bears are on a much different level than either the Panthers or the Falcons, and the Bucs will need to bring their A-game if they want to pull off the upset. If Tampa Bay can earn what would be its signature victory of the season, it will send a message to the rest of the NFC that the Bucs are for real and not to be taken lightly. If the Bucs lose, it will once again cast doubts over what their ceiling is this season. With the NFL's trade deadline coming up on Tuesday, how the Bucs fare against the Bears is likely to have a big impact on the organization's decision to be buyers or sellers. There are several players the Bucs could target at the deadline who could help them make a playoff push. Tampa Bay also has a few veterans who could fetch valuable draft picks if the team decides to sell. Sunday night's clash features the two best rushing offenses in the NFL. The Bucs average over 168 yards per game on the ground, while the Bears average over 150. Chicago leads the league with 17 rushing touchdowns. The first two of my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory are that the Bucs must stay committed to their running game and stop the Bears from running wild. Tampa has the NFL's stingiest rush defense but will have its hands full against the Bears. Last week, Chicago sent two first-round draft picks to the Tennessee Titans for stud defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who has already taken the defense to a new level. Simmons is a game-changer for the Bears, and his presence will make it much harder for Tampa's offense to find success on the ground. Or through the air. That is, if the Bucs even try to move the ball through the air. Last week, the Bucs became the first NFL team in over 50 years to win a game without completing a pass. The Bears aren't the Falcons. To beat Chicago, Tampa must have a more balanced attack. The Bears' passing offense, on the other hand, is elite. QB Caleb Williams may be the MVP favorite, if not for a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. The Bears have surrounding Williams with weapons. Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze give Chicago a dynamic WR duo. Colston Loveland is one of the best and most dangerous tight ends in the NFL. Tampa cornerbacks Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have played lights out all season and will once again have to step up against a terrific passing attack. This game will have serious playoff implications for the Bucs and could be the difference in whether the organization buys or sells at the deadline. Marching into Chicago and marching out with a win is a tough task for any team, especially one that seems to have only half an offense like the Bucs. I think the Bucs keep things close all game, but the Bears always seem to be just out of reach throughout. Prediction: Bears 30, Bucs 19

away.blurb: Buccaneers get an unexpected setback with Emeka Egbuka ruled out vs. Falcons The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will face the Chicago Bears in Week 9 on Sunday Night Football, and it’s shaping up to be their most difficult test of the season to date. The Bucs will need all hands on deck in order to pull off the road upset, but they may be shorthanded after some unexpected injury news. Left tackle Tristan Wirfs, Tampa Bay’s best and most important player, appeared on the injury report after missing practice on Thursday with a toe injury. If he can’t go on Sunday night, it would be devastating for the Buccaneers. Buccaneers can’t afford to lose Tristan Wirfs against the Bears Wirfs, a five-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro, is the anchor of the Buccaneers’ offensive line. He’s widely considered one of the best offensive tackles in the NFL , and he’s pivotal in protecting Baker Mayfield’s blind side and opening up holes in the running game. Wirfs currently owns the second-highest pass-blocking grade among all offensive tackles per Pro Football Focus. That kind of dependability is difficult to replace, especially against a ferocious Bears defense that has sacked opposing quarterbacks 22 times this season -- tied for fifth-most in the NFL.. It’s unclear when Wirfs’ toe injury took place. He finished Sunday’s game with no apparent issues or any mentions of an injury postgame. The severity is unclear, and Bucs fans arw holding their collective breath that this isn’t turf toe or a lingering injury that will impact Wirfs’ availability down the stretch. Whenever head coach Todd Bowles speaks to the media next, Wirfs’ status for Sunday night will be the first question he’s asked about. Ben Chukwuma could step in at left tackle if Tristan Wirfs can’t play vs. Bears Ben Chukwuma is Tampa Bay’s swing tackle, and he’s already filled in this season to replace Luke Goedeke in Week 7. He’d likely step in once again, this time at left tackle, if Wirfs can’t go on Sunday night. The Buccaneers have a lot of confidence in Chukwuma, and Bowles went as far as to say he has a future as an NFL starter . So at the very least, the Buccaneers have a capable backup if Wirfs is sidelined. But when going against a Super Bowl contending squad like the Bears, you don’t want to be without any of your best players. Wirfs currently owns the second-highest pass-blocking grade among all offensive tackles per Pro Football Focus. That kind of dependability is difficult to replace, especially against a ferocious Bears defense that has sacked opposing quarterbacks 22 times this season -- tied for fifth-most in the NFL.. It’s unclear when Wirfs’ toe injury took place. He finished Sunday’s game with no apparent issues or any mentions of an injury postgame. The severity is unclear, and Bucs fans arw holding their collective breath that this isn’t turf toe or a lingering injury that will impact Wirfs’ availability down the stretch. Whenever head coach Todd Bowles speaks to the media next, Wirfs’ status for Sunday night will be the first question he’s asked about. Ben Chukwuma could step in at left tackle if Tristan Wirfs can’t play vs. Bears Ben Chukwuma is Tampa Bay’s swing tackle, and he’s already filled in this season to replace Luke Goedeke in Week 7. He’d likely step in once again, this time at left tackle, if Wirfs can’t go on Sunday night. The Buccaneers have a lot of confidence in Chukwuma, and Bowles went as far as to say he has a future as an NFL starter . So at the very least, the Buccaneers have a capable backup if Wirfs is sidelined. But when going against a Super Bowl contending squad like the Bears, you don’t want to be without any of your best players. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Josh Allen and Buffalo's explosive offense face Brian Flores' dominant defense, while Carson Wentz replaces the injured Kyler Murray Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings host the Buffalo Bills . Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season after starting the year with six straight wins. The Vikings turn to Carson Wentz to start in place of Kyler Murray , who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Minnesota sports arguably the NFL's best defense, and it will be put to the test on Monday night against the Bills. Buffalo has won three consecutive games to improve to 6-1, and last week beat up on the Baltimore Ravens following an injury to Lamar Jackson on the Ravens' first snap of the game. Buffalo is in first place in the AFC East behind its efficient and explosive offense, which has helped offset a defense that has been highly vulnerable this year. Will the Vikings bounce back, or will the Bills continue to roll? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. How to watch Vikings vs. Bills live Date: Monday, Nov. 9 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: U.S. Bank Stadium (Minneapolis) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bills have the ball This is going to be one of the most fascinating matchups of the season, as arguably the NFL's best quarterback ( Josh Allen ) will do battle with arguably the NFL's best defensive play-caller (Brian Flores). We know the state of play: the Vikings are going to blitz on damn near every snap, and the Bills are going to have to figure out how in the world to deal with all the extra bodies the Vikings send against both the run and the pass. Last week, the Vikings totally shut down one of the best offenses in the league during the first half, holding the Lions to a mere 154 total yards (on 36 plays, an average of 4.3 per play) and only six points prior to the break. They frustrated Jared Goff and the passing game with their heavy blitzing and they limited Jahmyr Gibbs and company to a 25% rushing success rate. Buffalo has been one of the best running teams in the NFL, averaging 4.8 yards per carry, which ranks fourth in the league. The Bills can lean on James Cook, who, after leading the NFL in rushing last year, is actually averaging nearly six more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. Buffalo likes to get downhill runs with schemes like duo that create double teams inside, which is tough to do against the Vikings, but can lead to big gains if you can block them up front. Whether the Bills can do that is obviously another question. It's important to note that Allen has been blitzed on exactly a third of his dropbacks, per Tru Media, meaning he's faced the 11th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. He's 46 of 70 for 587 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions on those plays, and he's been sacked six times. That's all led to him checking in fourth in yards per attempt (8.4) and seventh in passing success rate (50.0%) but only 15th in EPA per dropback thanks to the interceptions. The Bills will need to get the ball out quickly against the blitz, which could mean underneath targets like Khalil Shakir and passing-down back Ty Johnson are heavily involved. It might be a lighter game for the likes of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox , as teams often keep their tight ends back in pass protection against Flores' blitz-happy defense. It might also be tough for DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to get open down the field, but there could be opportunities for big plays if the offensive line does hold up on any given snap. The Vikings have given up the occasional deep shot this year because they send so many men after the quarterback and it leaves them shorthanded on the back end at times. When the Vikings have the ball The Vikings have struggled to move the ball pretty much all season. Their 4.7 yards-per-play average is tied for third-worst in the NFL. Their 1.71 points-per-drive average is fifth-worst in the NFL. And their -0.14 expected points added per play average is second-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media. They've yet to gain more than 364 yards in any game, and they've been at 275 or fewer in five of their seven contests. They've scored more than 23 points just one time, and it was back in Week 1 when they had touchdown drives of 28, 1 and 14 yards late in the game against the Green Bay Packers . Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of Kyler Murray, who has completed 64.9% of his passes at an average of just 6.6 yards per attempt, with a mere five touchdown passes and three interceptions. Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of the run game, where the backs have combined to average south of 4.0 yards per carry. Jordan Mason missed four games, but it's not like he's been effective when he's been on the field, having averaged 3.9 yards a pop. Murray won't be on the field on Monday night. It'll be Carson Wentz under center in his place. Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in one-plus games in relief of Murray earlier this year. He seemed to have more command of the offense and more chemistry with Justin Jefferson than Murray does, at the very least. Jefferson went for eight catches for 92 yards and two scores during Wentz's relief appearance back in Week 1, and he was on the receiving end of seven of Wentz's 19 pass attempts in that game. (Wentz's start the following week came in a driving rainstorm in Chicago and doesn't provide much room for analysis.) If the Vikings can keep Wentz well-protected, there should be some opportunities for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson to find openings in what has been a very leaky back seven. The Bills have been solid against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry. Given the Vikings' struggles on the ground, it seems unlikely that they'll have much in the way of success running the ball here. You can't ask me to buy into this Minnesota offense right now — not even against Buffalo's leaky defense. We just saw the Vikings put up a relatively limp offensive performance against the Lions. And if there's a team out there that can run the ball on Minnesota the way the Lions did, it might be the Bills with Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo can win a low-ish scoring game here by doing just that. home.blurb: Buffalo's Thursday report includes five players who did not participate in practice, while five were limited and eight were full participants. The list also includes defensive back Jordan Hancock, who remains on injured reserve, and wide receiver Tyrell Shavers, who is on the physically unable to perform list. The biggest concern on the offensive line involves left tackle Dion Dawkins and right tackle Spencer Brown. Dawkins did not practice Thursday because of a rib injury, while Brown was limited with a back issue. Both starting tackles will be worth watching as the week progresses. Alec Anderson was also a non-participant with an ankle injury, meaning Buffalo's entire left side of the line was out. Buffalo's receiving group also has a few players dealing with injuries. Joshua Palmer did not practice because of a hamstring injury after leaving Sunday's win over Baltimore, while Keon Coleman was limited with a shoulder issue. DJ Moore, who recently returned from a shoulder injury, was also limited on Thursday and in a red non-contact. The good news, however, is that it was just for his shoulder after appearing to hyperextend his knee in Week 8. Tight end Dalton Kincaid was limited with a chest injury, while running back Ty Johnson missed practice because of an illness. The defensive side of the ball has its own concerns. Defensive tackle Greg Gaines did not practice with a calf injury, and cornerback Dee Alford was listed as a full participant with the ankle injury that kept him out last week. Ed Oliver, meanwhile, was a full participant with a knee injury. home.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he'll play or not. Kevin O'Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson's absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the 'playing through it' variety and don't seem like they'll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday.
